title: Partner publish sprint — async checklist & listing play notes
body:
Context and intent

Quick async notes from the partnership + marketplace sprint loop. This file is a thin, informal checklist and copy-sketch for a vendor-style marketplace tile (cloud marketplaces: AWS, Azure, GCP) and the partner co-publish flow. Use for handoff to PMM and the creative team; expect edits.

Top-level goals
- Produce a single source-of-truth checklist so integrations teams and partners can self-serve key publishing artifacts.
- Ship minimal listing copy + assets that meet vendor gating while preserving Redwood product voice.
- Identify risky dependencies early (KMS, SSO, billing SKU mapping).

High-level rollout plan (1 pager)
- Week 0: partner kickoff, define commercial SKU, confirm legal T&Cs and required attachments. Owner: Partner AE / Partner Ops.
- Week 1: assets & copy draft (this doc), technical acceptance checklist populated by eng. Owner: PMM + Solutions Eng.
- Week 2: vendor portal submission (beta) + internal QA (screenshots, billing test). Owner: Partner Ops.
- Week 3: vendor review, iterate on compliance asks (logs, data residency). Owner: Legal + Security.
- Week 4: live, monitor telemetry (tile CTR, trial signups, invalid usage errors). Owner: Growth + Analytics.

Minimum assets to assemble (Gating checklist)
- Short tile headline (<= 80 chars) — required by all vendors.
- 1–2 sentence descriptive summary (<= 350 chars).
- 600–800 word long description with 3–5 bullet feature list and sample use cases.
- Technical integration overview (1 A4): architecture diagram + bullet notes on networking, auth, and data flow.
- 3 screenshots (recommended sizes) + 1 product GIF or short demo clip.
- Logos: primary + white-on-dark + monochrome: each in PNG + SVG (transparent backgrounds).
- Customer trust signals: 1 customer quote + link to case study (if available).
- Pricing & SKU mapping: single publisher SKU and sandbox trial instructions.
- Legal attachments: DPA pointer, SOC2 link, contact for security review.

Sample tile copy (short headline + short description) — rough drafts
- Headline options (pick 1):
  • Redwood Inference — High-performance LLM inference (hosted + private)
  • Predictable, low-latency LLM serving for production apps
  • Fast, cost-effective inference: hosted API, Dedicated, Private

- Short description (option A):
  Deliver reliable, production-grade LLM inference with easy-to-use APIs, predictable pricing, and support for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Includes model catalog, token-level observability, and rollout controls.

- Short description (option B — partner-facing):
  Redwood Inference powers low-latency, secure LLM endpoints for product teams. Ship features faster with autoscaling dedicated pools, private VPC deployments, and built-in quality monitoring.

Long description skeleton (use this to expand to 600–800 words)
- Opening paragraph: problem statement (cost/latency/unreliable ops) + Redwood positioning (runtime + orchestration).
- Features section: bullets describing Hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Optimize toolkit, Console. For each bullet include a 1–2 sentence benefit statement.
- Integration notes: how to call APIs, supported auth flows, expected latencies (SLO ranges), and recommended SKU for trials.
- Security & compliance: KMS/HSM options, audit logging, SOC2, VPC/private network notes.
- Getting started: 3-step quickstart (signup, trial credits, sample request).
- Call-to-action: link to docs, contact partner AE, link to trial signup tile.

Technical acceptance checklist (solutions-eng input needed)
- Platform endpoints reachable from vendor validation region(s).
- Authentication flow documented: API keys + optional mTLS or OIDC handshake.
- Test vector: sample prompt + expected structure of tokens and time-to-first-byte (TTFB) target.
- KV-cache/streaming behavior documented for streaming APIs.
- Monetization: simulated billing flow in sandbox to validate SKU mapping.
- Deployment variant mapping: which Redwood model variants map to vendor listing options (e.g., rdx-small, rdx-large).
- Data handling: confirm logs retention policy and whether partner logs include PII; add redaction notes.

Ops & SRE preflight
- Observability hooks: ensure vendor can ingest basic telemetry or link to Redwood Console dashboard.
- Alerting thresholds: rate-limited errors, cold start spikes, 5xx bounce conditions.
- Fallback plan: fast-fail to cheaper variant or degrade to text-only output per policy.

Legal/compliance quick checks (must be attached before vendor submission)
- Active DPA + contact.
- SOC2 report link + pointer to compliance pack.
- Data residency statement for any region-specific listings.
- Export controls & sanctions check (vendor compliance team needs this).

Copy notes / tone guide (short)
- Voice: straightforward, engineering-first, product-focused. Avoid marketing hyperbole (no "AI that reads minds").
- Emphasize measurable outcomes: latency, cost per token, predictable throughput.
- Use plural "customers" not "users" when referencing business uses.

Open questions / decision log (notes-to-self)
- Do we publish a usage-based pricing snippet or only "contact for pricing" for initial listing? (AE prefers MOQ SKU for marketplace billing).
- Which customer quote is cleared for vendor publication? (waiting legal).
- Should we include model names or only "Redwood-verified open models" to avoid version churn?

Risks & mitigation matrix (short)
- Risk: Vendor requests full access to logs for review. Mitigation: provide sanitized sample logs + SOC2 + redaction doc.
- Risk: SKU mismatch causes billing disputes. Mitigation: run sandbox billing cycle and capture receipts; add line items mapping doc.
- Risk: Security review delays. Mitigation: surface critical checklist ASAP (KMS, SSO, audit logs) and assign security reviewer with 3-day SLA.

Action items (owners + quick dates)
- PMM: finalize headline + short description by 2025-11-18.
- Solutions Eng: complete technical acceptance checklist by 2025-11-19.
- Partner Ops: upload assets to vendor portal and submit by 2025-11-21.
- Legal: confirm customer quote clearance and DPA linkage by 2025-11-20.

Notes to reviewer
- This is intentionally lean — prioritize vendor gating items first (short headline, screenshots, SKU mapping). The long description can be polished by PMM after initial submission if vendor supports iterative updates.
- If you see anything missing, add as a single line under "Open questions" and tag owner in Slack #marketplace.

Appendix: useful snippet links
- Quickstart demo snippet to paste into vendor docs (paste-ready):
  "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>\" -d '{\"model\": \"rdx-1\", \"input\": \"Summarize the following...\"}'"

- Recommended screenshot checklist: login tile, console route view with per-route latency graph, embedding explorer, model selection modal.

End of notes — treat as working doc.
